assignments.description: Derive the Maxwell-Faraday equation: \oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = -\frac{d\Phi_B}{dt} and explain the physical significance of Lenz's Law according to CBSE Chapter 13.

rubric.criterion: Lenz's Law & Conservation of Energy Analysis

assignments.title: CBSE Class 10 Maths: Trigonometric Proofs & Frustum Modeling
assignments.description: Prove that \frac{\tan\theta}{1 - \cot\theta} + \frac{\cot\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} = 1 + \sec\theta \csc\theta and calculate the volume of a cone frustum of radii 4cm, 2cm and height 6cm.

submissions.content: Using Faraday Law of Induction: \mathcal{E} = -\frac{d\Phi_B}{dt}. The magnetic flux through an open surface bounded by loop C is \Phi_B = \int_S \mathbf{B} \cdot d\mathbf{A}. Applying Stokes Theorem yields \oint_C \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = -\frac{d}{dt} \int_S \mathbf{B} \cdot d\mathbf{A}. Lenz Law ensures conservation of energy.
submissions.feedback: Outstanding derivation! The application of Stokes theorem and physical interpretation of Lenz law are completely rigorous and well-formatted.

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Maths: Trigonometry, Mensuration & Geometry (Code 041)
tests.subject: Maths

questions.question: According to the CBSE Class 10 Trigonometry syllabus, what is the simplified value of \(\sin^2(63^\circ) + \sin^2(27^\circ)\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\sin(27^\circ) = \cos(90^\circ - 27^\circ) = \cos(63^\circ)\), we get \(\sin^2(63^\circ) + \cos^2(63^\circ) = 1\) using the standard identity.

questions.question: What is the Total Surface Area of a solid right circular cone of base radius \(r\) and slant height \(l\)?
questions.explanation: The total surface area is the sum of curved surface area \(\pi r l\) and base area \(\pi r^2\): \(\text{TSA} = \pi r (l + r)\).

questions.question: If the discriminant \(D = b^2 - 4ac = 0\) in quadratic equation \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), what is the nature of its roots?
questions.explanation: When discriminant \(D = 0\), the quadratic formula yields two real and equal roots \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Science: Light Reflection, Refraction & Electricity (Code 086)
tests.subject: Science (Physics)

questions.question: A concave mirror produces a three times magnified real image of an object placed at 10 cm in front of it. What is the image distance \(v\)?
questions.explanation: For a real inverted image, magnification \(m = -v/u = -3\). With \(u = -10\,\text{cm}\), we obtain \(v = 3u = 3(-10) = -30\,\text{cm}\).

questions.question: Which physical law states that the heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of current, resistance, and time \(H = I^2 R t\)?
questions.explanation: Joule's Law of Heating states that heat produced in a conductor is given by \(H = I^2 R t\).

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Science: Chemical Reactions & Acids, Bases, Salts (Code 086)
tests.subject: Science (Chemistry)

questions.question: What is the chemical formula and IUPAC name of Plaster of Paris (POP)?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}\), prepared by heating gypsum at 373 K.

questions.question: When zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid, which gas is liberated that burns with a pop sound?
questions.explanation: Reaction: \(\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\uparrow\). Hydrogen gas burns with a characteristic pop sound.

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Science: Life Processes & Heredity (Code 086)
tests.subject: Science (Biology)

questions.question: What is the basic functional structural filtration unit of the human kidney?
questions.explanation: Each kidney has a large number of filtration units called Nephrons, which filter blood to remove nitrogenous wastes like urea.

questions.question: In a cross between a pure tall pea plant (TT) and a short pea plant (tt), what is the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation according to Mendel's Monohybrid Cross?
questions.explanation: In the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross, the phenotypic ratio is 3 Tall : 1 Dwarf (Genotypic ratio is 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Social Science: Nationalism in India & Europe (Code 087)
tests.subject: Social Studies (History)

questions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi call off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
options: Due to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
Due to the Chauri Chaura violent incident in Gorakhpur
Due to the Simon Commission arrival
Due to the signing of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
questions.explanation: At Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur, a peaceful demonstration turned violent and a police station was burned, prompting Gandhi to halt the movement.

questions.question: Which historic pact between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1932 gave reserved seats in Provincial and Central Legislative Councils to Depressed Classes?
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact of September 1932 gave reserved seats to the Depressed Classes in general electorates rather than separate electorates.

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Social Science: Power Sharing & Federalism (Code 087)
tests.subject: Social Studies (Civics)

questions.question: Which constitutional tier of government was strengthened in India by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments in 1992?
options: Third Tier: Panchayati Raj and Municipalities (Decentralization)
questions.explanation: The 1992 amendments made decentralization effective by creating a mandatory third tier of local self-government (Panchayats and Municipalities).

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 English: Grammar & First Flight Prose (Code 184)
tests.subject: English

questions.question: In 'A Letter to God' by G.L. Fuentes, what did Lencho compare the heavy raindrops to?
questions.explanation: Lencho compared the big drops to ten-cent pieces and the small ones to five-cent coins ('new coins').

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect reported speech for: He said, 'I have completed my science assignment.'
options: He said that he has completed his science assignment.
He said that he had completed his science assignment.
He said that I had completed my science assignment.
He told that he had completed his science assignment.
questions.explanation: Present perfect ('have completed') shifts to past perfect ('had completed') and the pronoun shifts to 'he'.

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 Hindi: वाक्य भेद, वाच्य, समास व पद परिचय (Code 002/085)
tests.subject: Hindi

questions.question: 'जब वर्षा हुई, तब मोर नाचने लगे।' - यह वाक्य रचना की दृष्टि से किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
questions.explanation: जिस वाक्य में एक मुख्य उपवाक्य और एक या अधिक आश्रित उपवाक्य योजक (जब...तब) से जुड़े हों, वह 'मिश्र वाक्य' कहलाता है।

questions.question: 'बालक द्वारा पत्र लिखा जाता है।' - इस वाक्य में कौन-सा वाच्य है?
questions.explanation: यहाँ कर्म (पत्र) प्रधान है और क्रिया का लिंग-वचन कर्म के अनुसार है ('लिखा जाता है'), अतः यह 'कर्मवाच्य' है।

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 IT: RDBMS SQL Queries & Spreadsheets (Code 402)
tests.subject: IT (Information Technology)

questions.question: In a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS), what uniquely identifies each record/tuple in a table?
questions.explanation: A Primary Key is a column or set of columns that uniquely and non-null identifies each row in a database table.

questions.question: Which tool in LibreOffice Calc / Excel is used to determine what input value is needed to achieve a desired target output formula result?
questions.explanation: Goal Seek is a What-If Analysis tool that calculates the input value required to reach a specific target outcome.

tests.title: CBSE Class 10 PE: Anatomy, Sports Injuries & Yoga Wellness
tests.subject: PE (Physical Education)

questions.question: In sports medicine and first aid, what does the acronym 'PRICER' stand for when managing acute soft tissue injuries?
options: Practice, Run, Ice, Clean, Exercise, Recover
Protect, Rest, Ice, Compress, Elevate, Refer
Prevent, Rotate, Inject, Care, Examine, Relax
Push, Rub, Inhale, Cool, Extend, Rebound
questions.explanation: PRICER stands for Protect, Rest, Ice, Compress, Elevate, and Refer — the standard acute sports injury treatment protocol.

tests.title: Grade 10 Mathematics - Real Numbers Quiz
tests.topic: Chapter 1: Real Numbers (Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, Proofs of Irrationality of √2, √3, √5)

questions.question: What is the Prime Factorization of the number 5040?
Given that HCF(306, 657) = 9, find the LCM(306, 657).
questions.explanation: We know that for any two positive integers $a$ and $b$, $	ext{HCF}(a, b) 	imes 	ext{LCM}(a, b) = a 	imes b$. Therefore, $	ext{LCM}(306, 657) =  rac{306 	imes 657}{	ext{HCF}(306, 657)} =  rac{306 	imes 657}{9} = 34 	imes 657 = 22338$.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is irrational based on the standard proofs of irrationality?
questions.explanation: 3 + 2√5 is the sum of a rational number (3) and an irrational number (2√5), which is always irrational. √(9/16) = 3/4 (rational), 3.1416 is terminating (rational), and √4 + √9 = 2 + 3 = 5 (rational).

questions.question: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorization is unique, apart from:
options: the order in which the prime factors occur
the values of the prime factors themselves
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every composite number can be factorized as a product of prime numbers, and this factorization is unique, except for the order in which the prime factors occur (e.g., 2 × 3 = 3 × 2).

questions.question: In a proof by contradiction showing that √3 is irrational, what initial assumption is typically made?
options: √3 is a rational number of the form a/b where a and b are co-prime integers and b ≠ 0.
√3 can be expressed as a terminating decimal.
√3 is equal to the square of an integer.
questions.explanation: The standard proof by contradiction starts by assuming the opposite of what is to be proved—that √3 is a rational number, meaning it can be written as a/b in its simplest form where a and b are co-prime integers and b ≠ 0.

flashcardDecks.title: CBSE Class 10 Maths: Essential Board Formulas
flashcardDecks.subject: Maths

cards.front: What are the three fundamental Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities in CBSE Class 10?
cards.back:
1. \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1
2. 1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta
3. 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta

cards.front: What is the Quadratic Formula for roots of \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\)?
cards.back: \[ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \]

cards.front: What is the Volume of a Frustum of a Cone of height \(h\) and radii \(R, r\)?
State the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales's Theorem) in Triangles.
cards.back: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, it divides the two sides in the same ratio: \(\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{EC}\).

flashcardDecks.title: CBSE Class 10 Science: Board Exam Key Principles
flashcardDecks.subject: Science

cards.front: State Ohm's Law and its mathematical equation.
cards.back: The electric current \(I\) through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference \(V\) across its ends, provided temperature remains constant: \(V = IR\).

cards.front: What is the difference between Oxidation and Reduction in Chemical Reactions?
cards.back: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen/electrons. Reduction is the loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen/electrons.

cards.front: What is the Lens Formula for spherical lenses in Optics?
cards.back: \[ \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} \] where \(f\) is focal length, \(v\) is image distance, \(u\) is object distance.

cards.front: What are the raw materials and overall equation for Photosynthesis?
cards.back: \[ 6CO_2 + 6H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight, Chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \] Raw materials: Carbon Dioxide & Water.

flashcardDecks.title: Deck: Ray Optics & Reflection of Light
flashcardDecks.subject: General Study

cards.front: State the Law of Reflection and its geometric condition.
cards.back: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (\(\theta_i = \theta_r\)). Additionally, the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal vector all reside in the same plane.

cards.front: What is the mirror formula relating focal length \(f\), object distance \(u\), and image distance \(v\)?
cards.back: The mirror formula is \(\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}\).

cards.front: Write the formula for linear magnification \(m\) produced by a spherical mirror in terms of heights and distances.
cards.back: Linear magnification is given by \(m = \frac{h'}{h} = -\frac{v}{u}\), where \(h'\) is image height, \(h\) is object height, \(v\) is image distance, and \(u\) is object distance.

cards.front: Describe the characteristics of images formed by convex mirrors for any object position.
cards.back: Convex mirrors always produce images that are virtual, erect, and diminished, regardless of the object's position.

cards.front: What image properties are produced by a concave mirror when the object is placed beyond the principal focus?
cards.back: The concave mirror produces a real and inverted image.

flashcardDecks.title: Deck: Ray Optics & Reflection of Light
flashcardDecks.subject: General Study

cards.front: State the two primary laws of reflection.
cards.back: 1. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (\(\theta_i = \theta_r\)). 2. The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

cards.front: What is the mirror formula relating focal length \(f\), image distance \(v\), and object distance \(u\)?
cards.back: The mirror formula is \(\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}\).

cards.front: Define linear magnification \(m\) for a spherical mirror in terms of object and image coordinates.
cards.back: Linear magnification is the ratio of image height \(h'\) to object height \(h\), represented as \(m = \frac{h'}{h} = -\frac{v}{u}\).

cards.front: What type of image is consistently formed by a convex mirror regardless of object position?
cards.back: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image.

cards.front: Under what condition does a concave mirror produce a real and inverted image?
cards.back: A concave mirror produces a real and inverted image when the object is positioned beyond the principal focus.
